Hi Maya — thanks again for the call this morning. Recap + a few quick qualification items so we can pick the right commercial path and accelerate procurement:

- Primary use: document processing + summarization for customer support (low-latency inference at peak hours).
- Expected steady-state qps: ~30 concurrent with bursts to 150 for short windows.
- Data residency: US only for now.

Procurement/commercial questions (can you confirm?):
1) Purchase instrument: do you prefer company card (credit card) or will this need a formal PO + invoice process? If PO, does Orkestra require a purchase order number for initial pilots or only for contracted commitments?
2) Marketplace interest: are you open to buying via AWS Marketplace private offers? Any preference between AWS vs GCP Marketplace vs direct invoiced contract?
3) Contract signers: who will be the legal/finance approvers and is there an existing MSA we should expect to sign?
4) Timeline: ideal go-live for pilot is the first week of December — are there procurement blockers we should anticipate?

Next steps I propose: 
- You share quick answers to the 4 bullets above.
- I’ll attach a short procurement Q&A (one page) and a 2-slide marketplace primer so your procurement/finance team can see differences across buy flows.
- If PO is required, we’ll loop in our Finance Ops to provide net-30 invoicing and PO instructions; if card, we’ll provision access immediately.

Attaching: Orkestra_Procurement_QA.xlsx (one-tab) and Redwood_Marketplace_PRIMER.pdf (2 slides).

Thanks — want to flag Ben (cc) to help with billing/pricing details and Monica to coordinate onboarding and pilot SLOs.

Best,

Thanks, Tessa — great summary. Quick answers below to help you route this: 

1) Purchase instrument: For the pilot we can pay by company card (PO not required). For production we will likely need a PO + net-30 invoice process. Our procurement team typically requires a PO for commitments > $25k/year.
2) Marketplace interest: We prefer buying through AWS Marketplace if possible (private offer ideal). GCP Marketplace is a secondary option but we don’t have a strong preference today.
3) Contract signers: Legal will sign; finance will own billing. I’ll introduce our GC and procurement lead if we reach PO stage.
4) Timeline: Pilot in early December is fine — procurement for a PO would need a 3–4 week lead time once we decide to move to production.

I’ll loop in procurement email to take a look at the primer you attached.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Platform
Orkestra
